search_text: Contemporary Chinese-style Illustration · Landscapes Inspired by Classical Poetry Contemporary Chinese Illustration · Poetic Landscapes Artist unverified This group places a moment from a classical Chinese poem within a narrow, elongated frame. Dense canopies surround a river, path or white wall, and the eye moves slowly along pale openings before resting on solitary fishing, a pointing gesture, a moored boat, a dragonfly on a lotus tip or a flowering branch reaching over a wall. Its strength is the progression from large color areas to small narratives to fine texture, creating different experiences at a distance and up close. Blue-green and vermilion are the most striking colors, but blue-gray snow scenes, peach-pink blossom fields and green lotus ponds show how the same compositional language can carry different seasons. As posters, the series is coherent and its subjects are easy to read; as poetic illustrations, the splendor and exuberance of some images can also diminish the chill, melancholy or contrast between aliases: 当代武侠人物插画：浮世绘武者绘与浪纹的视觉借鉴，融合夸张透视、动作海报构图和仿旧纸纹
summary: 这组竖幅人物插画以黑色轮廓、有限的哑光设色、卷浪、竖排题签和米黄旧纸效果建立浮世绘感，再把手掌、巨剑、头发和衣带推向观者，形成现代武侠动作海报的冲击力。系列统一性很强，乔峰的掌与龙、周伯通的双手与竹、黄药师的笛与海浪、杨过的剑与雕，又用不同物件提示人物身份。最值得学习的是“大动作—大色面—流动细线”的组织；主要不足是满幅裂纹与碎斑削弱疏密，部分黑发、衣袍、羽翼和山石相互粘连。四张中，黄药师的动静对照与色彩分区最突出，周伯通的表情与明暗分离较鲜明。
search_text: Ukiyo-e-inspired · Wuxia Characters Ukiyo-e-inspired Wuxia Characters Artist unverified These vertical character illustrations create an ukiyo-e-inspired appearance through black contours, a limited matte palette, curling waves, vertical title cartouches and beige aged-paper effects. Palms, great swords, hair and sashes then project toward the viewer, producing the impact of contemporary wuxia action posters. The series is highly coherent, while distinct objects suggest each character’s identity: Qiao Feng’s palm and dragon, Zhou Botong’s hands and bamboo, Huang Yaoshi’s flute and waves, and Yang Guo’s sword and eagle. The most useful lesson is the organization of major action, broad color areas and flowing fine lines. The main limitation is that all-over cracks and mottling weaken variation in density, while some black hair, robes, wings and rocks merge. Of the four images, Huang Yaoshi’s contrast of stillness and movement and color divisions stand out most; Zhou Botong’s expression and light–dark separation are also especially clear. 版画与绘本
